# Monte

> Monte (https://monte.markets) is a free site for learning business statistics, one idea at a time. Fourteen topics from data and sampling to multiple regression, each with a plain explanation, a worked example, an interactive lab and timed drills. Games teach the same ideas with real data, and every formula is on one sheet with a worked example.

The lesson content is also published as static JSON (no key needed). Free to use with a link to monte.markets. Updated 2026-11-06.

## Start here

- [Home](https://monte.markets/): what the site is and where to begin
- [Study](https://monte.markets/study/): learn, practice and solve, with progress kept in the browser
- [All topics](https://monte.markets/learn/): the fourteen topics in teaching order
- [Formula sheet](https://monte.markets/learn/formulas/): every formula with a worked example
- [Glossary](https://monte.markets/learn/terms/): terms in plain words, each with an example
- [Play](https://monte.markets/play/): games that each hide one statistics idea
- [Why statistics](https://monte.markets/story/): the case for learning it
- [How it's built](https://monte.markets/built/): the stack, the data sources and the math

## Topics

- [Data and sampling](https://monte.markets/learn/data/): Statistics is using data to make a decision. You can't check everyone, so you check a slice (the sample) and let it speak for the whole group (the population).
- [Where is the middle](https://monte.markets/learn/center/): Mean is the average. Median is the middle once sorted. Mode is the most common.
- [How spread out is it](https://monte.markets/learn/spread/): Range is biggest minus smallest. Standard deviation is the typical distance from the average; in finance, risk.
- [Probability rules](https://monte.markets/learn/prob/): Or: add, then subtract the overlap. And: multiply. Given: count only inside what you were told.
- [Random variables and expected value](https://monte.markets/learn/rv/): A random variable is a number that depends on chance. Its expected value is the long-run average, weighted by probability.
- [Two variables: covariance, correlation, portfolios](https://monte.markets/learn/two/): Covariance asks whether two things move together. Correlation rescales it from −1 to +1.
- [Counting and the binomial](https://monte.markets/learn/count/): Repeat a yes-or-no try n independent times with the same chance p: the count of yeses is binomial, mean np, variance np(1 − p).
- [Poisson: counts per unit](https://monte.markets/learn/poisson/): Poisson counts events in a fixed window when they arrive independently at a steady average rate λ.
- [The normal curve and z](https://monte.markets/learn/normal/): The normal is the bell. Measure in SDs from the mean, z = (y − μ) / σ, and any normal becomes the standard one.
- [Sampling distributions and the CLT](https://monte.markets/learn/clt/): Sample means have their own distribution. The Central Limit Theorem says it is near normal for big n, centered on μ, with spread σ / √n (the standard error).
- [Confidence intervals and sample size](https://monte.markets/learn/ci/): A confidence interval is your estimate plus or minus a margin: estimate ± critical value × standard error.
- [Hypothesis tests](https://monte.markets/learn/test/): A hypothesis test asks: would this data be surprising if nothing were going on?
- [Simple regression](https://monte.markets/learn/reg/): Regression fits the line with the smallest squared misses. Slope: how much y moves per unit of x.
- [Multiple regression](https://monte.markets/learn/mreg/): Several x's. Each coefficient is one x's effect holding the others fixed.

## Open data

- [index.json](https://monte.markets/api/v1/index.json): the list of endpoints, the license and the date
- [topics.json](https://monte.markets/api/v1/topics.json): every topic with its idea, why it matters, formulas, hook, trap and URL
- [formulas.json](https://monte.markets/api/v1/formulas.json): the formula sheet by topic, with worked examples
- [terms.json](https://monte.markets/api/v1/terms.json): the glossary
- [sources.json](https://monte.markets/api/v1/sources.json): recommended free courses, books and videos
